answer:
The best chain on garnet is QB7-QB12-QB11. QB12 sits in the middle.

How I picked it: I read the current default calibration set of the real garnet QPU (f81c45da-6e73-4b5d-a0fe-72c75635fade, measured 2026-10-21 at 16:42Z). That set lists 28 calibrated CZ pairs, and each pair has an interleaved randomized benchmarking (IRB) CZ fidelity. I checked every chain of 3 connected qubits and multiplied the two CZ fidelities along it. The pair QB12-QB7 has fidelity 0.99802. The pair QB12-QB11 has fidelity 0.99869. Their product is 0.99671, which is the highest of all chains. The next best is QB12-QB11-QB16 at 0.99469.

What I ran: I ran a 3-qubit GHZ circuit on garnet:mock with 200 shots, as one job (ID 01a160a4-460c-7078-99e0-af490fbb2937). The circuit uses only native gates on exactly those 3 qubits. QB12 is put into an equal mix of 0 and 1. Two CZ gates, one on QB12-QB7 and one on QB12-QB11, with single-qubit rotations around them, copy that state onto the two end qubits. Then all 3 qubits are measured. I read the circuit back from the server. It has 2 CZ gates and measures QB7, QB12, QB11 in that order.

Counts, with bits in the order QB7, QB12, QB11: 000 = 42, 001 = 46, 110 = 56, 111 = 56.

What the numbers show: A perfect quantum computer running this circuit gives only 000 and 111, each about half the time. I checked that with a noiseless simulation of the exact submitted circuit. The 3 qubits are entangled, so they always agree. The mock counts do not follow this pattern, because the garnet:mock service returns random results that do not depend on the circuit. So this job checks that the circuit is valid on that chain. It does not test the physics. To see the real 000 and 111 pattern, you would run the same circuit on the real garnet QPU. That would cost credits. The principle is that a GHZ state links several qubits so that measuring one tells you the others. The quality of that link depends on the CZ gates, so choosing the pair with the highest fidelity product should give the cleanest GHZ state on real hardware.
